title: Certificates of Deposit: when a grace-period jumbo top-up is written, and when nothing is written
content:
## Scope

This rule decides, for a request by the owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate in its grace period to add just enough money to earn the jumbo bonus on renewal, whether the top-up is written at its size or not at all.

## Rule

1. **Written only when.** A top-up is written only when the certificate's reconciled principal is below the jumbo threshold and the top-up fits both the room left under the tier's most added per grace period and the current balance of the source account.
2. **Otherwise nothing.** Otherwise nothing is written.
3. **Never cut down.** A top-up is never cut down to fit: where it does not fit either limit, nothing is written rather than a smaller deposit.

## Decision table

| Principal below the jumbo threshold | Top-up fits the room left under the grace total | Top-up fits the source account balance | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Written at the top-up size |
| Yes | No | Any | Nothing written; not reduced |
| Yes | Any | No | Nothing written; not reduced |
| No | Any | Any | Nothing written |

## Cases (hypothetical figures)

- The top-up works out at 1500.00; the room left under the grace total is 20000.00 and the source account holds 1200.00. The top-up does not fit the account balance, so nothing is written; a deposit of 1200.00 is not made in its place.
- The reconciled principal is already exactly at the threshold. It is not below the threshold, so nothing is written.

## Points of judgement

**The source account cannot cover the whole top-up. Is whatever the account holds taken instead?**
No. A top-up is never cut down to fit, and nothing is written.
